Requirement: Every enquiry has one current stage and a dated history from first contact to order, visible to everyone who works on it.
What the vendor must show: Open an enquiry from last quarter and show every call, quotation and stage change on it, with who did each and when.

Requirement: History from the old CRM and spreadsheets is imported and checked row by row; a row that can't be matched to exactly one customer is held for a person, not guessed.
What the vendor must show: Ask how many rows of your old data would be imported, how many held for review, and how a held row is resolved.

Requirement: Quotations are generated as PDFs in the company's own format, with revisions numbered and kept, from the same items and rates the order will use.
What the vendor must show: Revise a quotation twice and show all three versions, then convert the accepted one into an order without retyping a line.

Requirement: Follow-ups are planned with a date and an owner, and overdue ones are listed for each salesperson and their manager.
What the vendor must show: Show this week's due and overdue follow-ups for one salesperson, as their manager sees them.

Requirement: Win/loss, funnel, order and payment reports are computed from the enquiry, order and payment records themselves, not from a separate spreadsheet.
What the vendor must show: Pick one figure on the funnel report and drill down to the records that make it up.

Requirement: Where the group has more than one company, each quotation and invoice is issued under the company chosen for it, with that company's letterhead, logo and GSTIN, from one shared customer list.
What the vendor must show: Raise one invoice for each company to the same customer and show both letterheads and GSTINs.

Requirement: Shortfalls against orders and bills of materials become purchase requests automatically, after stock and usable remnants are counted.
What the vendor must show: Release an order that needs more than is in stock and show the purchase request it creates, net of what's available.

Requirement: Each supplier receives a private link by email or WhatsApp to enter rates and delivery dates, with no account to create.
What the vendor must show: Send an RFQ to two suppliers, enter their rates on the links, and compare the quotes side by side.

Requirement: Choosing a supplier's quote drafts the purchase order with the quoted rates and dates, without retyping.
What the vendor must show: Accept one supplier quote and open the purchase order it drafts.

Requirement: Every supplier bill is matched against its purchase order and the goods receipt before it is approved for payment; differences in quantity or rate are flagged.
What the vendor must show: Receive less than was ordered, enter the supplier's bill for the full quantity, and show the mismatch flagged before approval.

Requirement: Every vendor and freight charge is compared with its agreed reference rate, and anything above it is flagged for a person.
What the vendor must show: Enter a freight trip above the agreed rate and show where it is flagged and who sees it.

Requirement: Suppliers registered as micro or small enterprises are marked, and each of their bills shows its due date under the MSMED Act, with overdue bills listed before the year closes.
What the vendor must show: Mark a supplier as a micro enterprise, enter a bill, and show its due date and the list of MSME bills nearing or past it.
Law: MSMED Act, 2006, section 15 (with Income-tax Act, 2025, section 37(2)(g))

Requirement: Year-end reports list MSME amounts paid after the section 15 time limit separately, so the accountant can treat them correctly in the tax computation.
What the vendor must show: Show the year-end list of MSME bills paid late, with bill date, acceptance date and payment date.
Law: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 37(2)(g) (formerly section 43B(h) of the 1961 Act)

Requirement: Stock is tracked by each physical unit that is picked and shipped (a reel, a box, a plate), each with its own number and label, not only as a total quantity.
What the vendor must show: Receive two reels of the same part with different quantities and show each as its own unit with its own label.

Requirement: Stock moves in, out and between stores by scanning with a phone camera or scanner, not by typing codes.
What the vendor must show: Move three units between stores by scanning them with a phone, then show the move in both stores' records.

Requirement: Stock is held in more than one store or site, including a partner's, and every move between them is logged unit by unit.
What the vendor must show: Show stock for one item split across two stores, and the log of the last move between them.

Requirement: Stock is reserved against each customer order line; a reserved unit shows as reserved when scanned, and shipping it elsewhere needs a manager's override.
What the vendor must show: Reserve a unit for one order, then try to ship it on another and show the block and the override.

Requirement: Stock entries made by staff wait for a manager's approval before they change stock; a manager's own entries go through at once.
What the vendor must show: Enter a receipt as store staff, show it pending, approve it as a manager, and show the stock change only then.

Requirement: Stock balances are worked out from the movements themselves, not kept as a separate running total that can drift.
What the vendor must show: Show the movements behind one item's balance and that they add up to it exactly.

Requirement: Bills of materials kept in Excel are imported as they are, matched to the item master and grouped into assemblies; a likely typo is suggested, never silently corrected.
What the vendor must show: Import one of your real BOM sheets and show how each unmatched line is handled.

Requirement: A released bill of materials is frozen as a version that purchase and stores work from; later edits make a new version.
What the vendor must show: Release a BOM, edit a line, and show the released version unchanged and the edit as a new version.

Requirement: At each cut, what was used and the usable remnant are recorded; remnant weights come from dimensions and density, and remnants return to stock to be matched to waiting BOM lines before anything is bought.
What the vendor must show: Cut a plate, record the remnant, and show it back in stock with its weight and offered against a waiting BOM line.

Requirement: Each job is costed from the material and labour actually recorded against it, with each used piece costed by its share of the source piece.
What the vendor must show: Show one finished job's cost, and the issues and work logs behind each line of it.

Requirement: For each job or milestone the system shows what it is waiting on (material, drawing, approval, payment), worked out fresh each time it is opened.
What the vendor must show: Open a delayed job and show what it is waiting on, then clear the blocker and show the status change by itself.

Requirement: Material test certificates are kept once, in a bank, and linked to each piece of material and each product they apply to.
What the vendor must show: Show one certificate and every product it has been used for.

Requirement: The system may suggest which certificate belongs to which part, but a link that ends up in statutory paperwork is made only after a person confirms it.
What the vendor must show: Show a suggested certificate link waiting for confirmation, and that it doesn't appear in any document until confirmed.

Requirement: Statutory quality documents (for example a boiler's IBR folder) are assembled from the records already in the system, not compiled by hand.
What the vendor must show: Generate the statutory folder for one finished product and check each certificate in it against the material used.

Requirement: For goods moving with a consignment value above ₹50,000, the e-way bill is generated from the invoice and dispatch record, without retyping into the portal.
What the vendor must show: Dispatch a consignment above ₹50,000 and show the e-way bill details produced from the invoice.

Requirement: Packing lists, invoices and certificates for a dispatch are produced from the same order and released to the customer as they are issued.
What the vendor must show: Dispatch part of an order and show the packing list, invoice and certificates for exactly what left.

Requirement: Suppliers record each dispatch on their link (lines, quantities, transporter, vehicle, LR number, photos), so stores see what is on the way.
What the vendor must show: Record a supplier dispatch on the link and show it in stores' incoming list.

Requirement: Every transaction in the books has an audit trail: an edit log of each change with the date it was made, which cannot be switched off.
What the vendor must show: Enter a purchase bill, change its amount, and show the edit log with the old value, the new value, the user and the time; then show there is no setting to disable it.

Requirement: The audit trail has been on, without gaps, for every financial year from 1 April 2023, including for data migrated from an older system.
What the vendor must show: Show the audit trail for an entry made before the switch to the new system, and the first entry after it.

Requirement: Where aggregate turnover has exceeded ₹5 crore in any year since 2017-18, B2B invoices, credit notes and debit notes get an IRN from the invoice registration portal before they are issued.
What the vendor must show: Issue a B2B invoice and show the IRN and signed QR code returned from the IRP on the printed invoice.
Law: Notification No. 13/2020–Central Tax, as amended by No. 10/2023–Central Tax (under CGST Rules, rule 48(4))

Requirement: Where annual aggregate turnover is ₹10 crore or more, every e-invoice, credit note and debit note is reported to the IRP within 30 days of its date, and the system warns before that window closes.
What the vendor must show: Show the list of invoices not yet reported to the IRP, with the days left for each.

Requirement: GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B are prepared from the sales, purchase and stock records already in the system, and input tax credit is reconciled against them.
What the vendor must show: Produce last month's GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B from the system and tie one line of each back to its invoice.

Requirement: GST rates by HSN, TDS rates and payroll slabs come from one registry that a person verifies, used by every module, not typed into each transaction.
What the vendor must show: Change a rate in the registry with an effective date and show transactions before and after it using the right rate.

Requirement: Where the business is a buyer with turnover above ₹10 crore in the previous year, purchases from a seller beyond ₹50 lakh in the year attract TDS, and the system tracks each seller's running total and deducts from the right bill.
What the vendor must show: Show one supplier's purchases this year against the ₹50 lakh threshold and the bill on which deduction started.
Law: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1), Table, Sl. No. 8(ii) and its Note

Requirement: A period whose returns have been filed is locked; any later correction goes in as a dated adjustment, with the audit trail intact.
What the vendor must show: Lock last month, try to edit an invoice in it, and show the block and the correct adjustment route.

Requirement: Bank statement lines are matched to entries automatically only when the match is unique both ways; everything else goes to a person.
What the vendor must show: Import a statement with two receipts of the same amount and show that neither is matched automatically.

Requirement: Purchases under reverse charge are marked, and the tax payable on them is computed and shown in the returns.
What the vendor must show: Enter a reverse-charge purchase and show the tax liability it creates in the return.

Requirement: Fixed assets are kept in a register with cost, date put to use and depreciation, posted to the ledger.
What the vendor must show: Add an asset, run depreciation for the year, and show the ledger entries it made.

Requirement: If Tally stays as the books, approved invoices post into TallyPrime as vouchers automatically, and each posted voucher is checked against Tally's own data so one deleted inside Tally is flagged.
What the vendor must show: Approve an invoice, show the voucher in TallyPrime, delete it in Tally, and show it flagged as unconfirmed after the next sync.

Requirement: Pay is computed from attendance, rates and advances recorded during the month, never typed as a final figure.
What the vendor must show: Show one worker's month: days present, rate, advances, and the pay the system worked out.

Requirement: Who worked on which order, and on which part, is logged daily, so labour shows up in job costs.
What the vendor must show: Log a day's work for two people on one order and show it in that order's cost.

Requirement: PF, ESI, professional tax and income-tax slabs come from the verified rate registry and are applied by rule, not typed per employee.
What the vendor must show: Show the deductions for one salaried employee and the registry entries they came from.

Requirement: Customers sign in to see each of their orders as plain-language stages worked out from what each department records, never typed for the customer.
What the vendor must show: Sign in as a customer, open an order, then move it forward internally and show the customer's view change.

Requirement: The customer portal shows a customer only their own orders and documents; stock levels, other customers and internal prices are never exposed.
What the vendor must show: Sign in as one customer and try to open another customer's order by changing its number in the address.

Requirement: Drawings, certificates, packing lists and invoices appear to the customer as they are released, and drawings can be approved or uploaded there.
What the vendor must show: Release a drawing, approve it as the customer, and show the approval recorded on the order.

Requirement: Every figure on every report can be opened to show the transactions it was computed from.
What the vendor must show: Pick a figure on the owner's dashboard and open the records behind it.

Requirement: An AI assistant answers from fixed look-ups in code; it never writes a number itself, and any written answer containing a number not in the data is dropped.
What the vendor must show: Ask the assistant this month's sales in plain English and in Hinglish, then compare its answer with the sales report.

Requirement: AI reads purchase invoices, bills of entry, purchase orders and bank statements into the system, and a person approves each one before anything posts.
What the vendor must show: Upload five of your own documents and show the fields read, the corrections needed, and that nothing posted before approval.

Requirement: Drawings, certificates, past quotations and decisions are searchable in plain words, and each answer shows the document it came from.
What the vendor must show: Search for a past quotation by what was quoted, not its number, and open the source.

Requirement: The ERP connects to TallyPrime through an agent on the Tally PC (Tally's gateway only listens there), with vouchers pushed and outstandings synced back on a fixed schedule.
What the vendor must show: Show the agent running beside TallyPrime and the last sync times for vouchers and masters.

Requirement: Receivables with ageing, payables, registers, cash, bank and stock are copied out of TallyPrime into the business system on a schedule, and show the last sync when Tally is off.
What the vendor must show: Show receivables ageing in the ERP and the time of its last sync from Tally.

Requirement: The ERP sends B2B invoices to the invoice registration portal and stores the IRN and signed QR code returned.
What the vendor must show: Generate an IRN from the ERP for a test invoice and show the QR code on the print.

Requirement: The ERP generates e-way bills through the NIC e-way bill system from dispatch records.
What the vendor must show: Generate an e-way bill for a test dispatch and show its number on the dispatch record.

Requirement: Bank statements are imported from the bank's PDF or file, read into lines, and offered for reconciliation.
What the vendor must show: Import one month's statement from your bank and show the lines it read.

Requirement: Sheets people already keep (BOMs, price lists, opening stock) import through the interface, with each problem row shown rather than silently skipped.
What the vendor must show: Import a sheet with one bad row and show how the bad row is reported.

Requirement: Links that suppliers and customers act on (RFQs, quotations, reminders) can be sent on WhatsApp as well as email.
What the vendor must show: Send an RFQ link to a supplier on WhatsApp from the system.

Requirement: When the connection drops, work in progress isn't lost: syncs retry by themselves, and a real error (a missing ledger, a rejected voucher) waits for a person.
What the vendor must show: Pull the network cable during a sync and show what happens to the queued entries when it's back.

Requirement: What each role can see is enforced by the system itself, not just hidden on screen; staff can be refused bank data entirely.
What the vendor must show: Sign in as staff and try to open a bank page directly by its address.

Requirement: Agents and integrations sign in with their own machine identities, separate from people, so their actions are traceable and revocable.
What the vendor must show: Show the list of machine identities and revoke one.

Requirement: Logins created at setup must have their passwords changed on first sign-in.
What the vendor must show: Sign in with a newly created user and show the forced password change.

Requirement: Stores, site and sales staff can do their daily tasks on a phone: scanning stock, marking attendance, checking an order.
What the vendor must show: Do a stock scan and mark attendance on a phone, in front of you.

Requirement: All business data can be exported at any time in standard formats, during the contract and at its end.
What the vendor must show: Ask for a full export of the demo data and open it in Excel.

Requirement: Personal data of staff, customers and contacts is protected with reasonable security safeguards, and a breach can be traced and reported.
What the vendor must show: Ask who can see employees' personal details, how access is logged, and how a breach would be detected and reported.
Law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, section 8(5)

Requirement: Support requests have a stated response time in the contract, and the vendor has written documentation that lets another developer take the system over.
What the vendor must show: Ask for the response time in writing, and to see the system document for one of their live systems.

Requirement: The contract states who owns the source code and the software, and what the buyer gets: the code itself, or a licence to use the system for a stated term.
What the vendor must show: Ask for the ownership clause in writing before the build starts.

Requirement: Work is priced in fixed phases, each quoted before it starts, rather than an open-ended hourly bill.
What the vendor must show: Ask for the phase plan with a fixed price and a go-live date for each phase.

Requirement: A change is written down, priced and agreed before it is built, never billed after the fact.
What the vendor must show: Ask how the last change on one of their projects was priced and approved.

Requirement: The AMC states what it covers (licence, hosting, fixes, small changes), what it costs per year, and what is quoted separately.
What the vendor must show: Ask for the AMC scope and price in writing, and an example of something it doesn't cover.
